analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 18...Copper WEBCAST 9am (replay available), ... 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Copper is trading poorly. The dollar is up (DXY 103.76) and the US 10-year yield is 5.09%. The author hears margin calls in base and precious metals and sees no single catalyst overnight.
China copper open interest rose 5% (30k lots) on light volume, similar to mid-2025 levels. The author is watching China closely because it has traded badly.

China physical copper premiums keep rising to record highs. SHFE is short, meaning open interest exceeds the metal available for delivery. Warrant stocks are rising from a very low base, and the arbitrage points to metal moving from CMX into Shanghai (the author is watching NOLA).

China, CTAs and Druckenmiller are positioned short copper. The author notes Druckenmiller said he was trying not to lose money, not that he sold the day before, and suspects traders may start covering at these levels.

On the medium-term copper benchmark, the author expects treatment charges to go negative. CRU says -$50 to -$100/t, noting top smelters stay profitable at -$118/t. The author has heard -$50 to -$150/t, and sources on the ground say either side of -$100/t is achievable. This would squeeze marginal smelters and show up in cathode production. Who sets the benchmark is unclear, with Antofagasta or Codelco seen as unlikely and some suggesting Freeport.
The author sees the power grid as the place to look for real copper demand. China has the generation capacity and needs connection and distribution. 600406.CH is named as a stock to watch.
China trade data: copper output +1.8% y/y at 1.22mt, zinc -9.7% y/y at 604kt, rare earth exports +5.5% y/y at 11kt and alumina exports +39.9% y/y at 250kt.

China Basic Materials Monitor: volatility in metal prices and the copper physical premium caused end-user order books to be pushed back for the first time in months. Domestic copper scrap disruption is deep and unchanged, and further smelter output cuts remain a risk. First-half November demand was 2% higher y/y for copper and aluminium and 2% to 10% lower y/y for cement, flat steel and construction steel.

Anglo American CEO says that if the MMG sale of the Brazilian nickel business is prohibited, Barro Alto and Codemin ferronickel volumes would be withdrawn from the market permanently. Brazil told the European Commission its review is unwelcome interference. Dec 21 is the date to watch.

BHP is reported to be discussing the sale of West Musgrave (nickel, copper). The author sees the possible sale of East Coast coal assets, which is not ruled out, as the more interesting item for BHP and Glencore.

Glencore: ERG will split into two businesses. Mutalip is the buyer of Kazzinc, a 70% stake that consensus values at $4.0 to $4.5bn (FT said up to $5bn). The Glencore CEO said in October it would complete in 30 to 60 days. Zinc has been the best base metal YTD, and zinc treatment charges are moving the same direction as copper while staying positive.

First Quantum: the company announced formal talks on the Cobre Panama contract will start after the president agreed with his ministers' recommendation. The author says the focus is now the economics of the new contract and has heard ministers target year-end. At C$30 the stock trades on 3.5x/2.5x EV/EBITDA with Cobre fully ramped (2028/29) and 6.3x/5.7x without it.

First Quantum pipeline: TacaTaca is valued at $7bn capex and $11bn NAV (100%), with first production in 2035 (FID late 2027, possibly production by 2032). Existing operations are modelled to rise from 375kt to 450kt by 2028. The author calls the stock a top-of-page ask in copper.

Mineral Resources AGM: shareholders pushed back over exit payments and a $3m bonus. Northern Star AGM: management said it will not entertain transaction structures that give away near-term execution upside without a premium.

SSE H1 2027 adjusted EPS of 65.5p was in line with the 64p to 68p trading statement range. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of 168p to 193p is unchanged against Bloomberg consensus of 185.6p, and capex is expected to be over £5bn.

Severn Trent H1 2027 PBIT beat GS expectations by 2%, helped by a £14m property sale. The EPS beat reflects timing of interest costs between H2 and H1. GS stays Sell with a 3,116p 12-month price target.

China A-shares ended with small gains in range-bound trading. Turnover fell below RMB 1.4tn, the lowest since July 2025. Chip-control headlines drive sector performance, and GS China Domestic AI rose 3.78%. Small and micro caps underperformed.

market_movers.rationale: GS remains Sell on Severn Trent after H1 2027 results. PBIT beat expectations by 2%, helped by a £14m property sale, and the EPS beat reflects interest cost timing.

First Quantum announced formal talks on the Cobre Panama contract and the author says a reopening is getting closer. The author calls it a top-of-page ask in copper and notes ministers are reported to target year-end.

earnings_insights: SSE H1 2027 adjusted EPS reported at 65.5p, in line with the company's trading statement range of 64p to 68p. Full-year 2026/27 adjusted EPS guidance of 168p to 193p is reiterated, against Bloomberg consensus of 185.6p.

Severn Trent H1 2027 reported results were a 2% PBIT beat versus GS expectations, helped by a £14m property sale. The EPS beat versus GS expectations is driven mostly by interest cost timing between H2 and H1.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Output is growing modestly while scrap disruption and smelter cut risk persist.
A sharp y/y fall in zinc output.
Alumina exports are sharply higher y/y.
Copper and aluminium demand is slightly higher y/y while cement, flat steel and construction steel are 2% to 10% lower.
Negative treatment charges would squeeze marginal smelters and reduce cathode production.

risk_factors: Rising dollar and US rates are pressuring copper.
Further output cuts by Chinese copper smelters are a risk, with domestic scrap disruption deep and unchanged.
Price volatility and the physical premium are causing end-user order book pushback in China.
Anglo American says the alternative to the MMG nickel sale is not the status quo, with ferronickel volumes withdrawn permanently if the deal is prohibited.
Cobre Panama contract economics and timing are uncertain for First Quantum.
vol_and_positioning: The author hears margin calls in base and precious metals, with no obvious trigger overnight.
China has been getting short copper, CTAs are positioned the same way, and Druckenmiller has said he is short copper.
China copper open interest rose 5% (30k lots) on volumes as light as mid-2025 levels.
SHFE is short metal, with more open interest than metal to deliver against it. Physical premiums in China are at record highs.
The author notes a historical back test but gives no details of its content.
geopolitical: Brazil told the European Commission that its review of Anglo American's sale of a Brazilian nickel mine to MMG is unwelcome interference. Dec 21 is the date to watch.
Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data center chips to China, despite US government approval last year to sell a version of it.
Reuters reports the US will move forward with a ban on China optical transceivers despite US hyperscaler pushback.
First Quantum Cobre Panama: the president agreed with his ministers' recommendation and formal talks on a new contract will commence.

tension_points.bull_case: China physical premiums are at record highs, SHFE open interest exceeds deliverable metal, warrant stocks are rising and traders may start covering. The author suspects Druckenmiller's comment does not mean he sold the day before.
tension_points.bear_case: A higher dollar and 10-year yield, margin calls in base and precious metals, light China volumes and short positioning by China, CTAs and Druckenmiller all pressure copper.
